name: Symbiosis (cells bond with strangers)
description: A sunlit, low-food world where cells can bond to ANY cell that touches them (not just their own babies), with a stickiness gene deciding how readily. Nothing rewards it: bonded cells simply share energy, so a mixed colony can help both partners (mutualism) or let one drain the other (parasitism), and selection decides. In our tests stickiness faded and no mixed colony survived, though one-lineage colonies sometimes grew to the 16-cell cap from no bonding at all. Mixed colonies are counted in the colonies readout. Color the dots by Colony size.
